newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds up on hopes for interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds up on hopes for interest rate cut.

text.p: Israeli bonds rose on Sunday on expectations of a cut in interest rates and lower yields, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.09 pct to 106.19
Volume including Makams was 131 million shekels.

"Prices were up quite sharply on long-term CPI-linked bonds with a mixed trend for short-term and medium-term CPI-linked bonds," said Adam Reuter, managing director of the Financial Immunities consultancy.
"The rises in the long-term bonds are an indication that speculators are entering the market because interest rates are expected to go down," he said.
The base rate has been 13.9 percent since the end of February. The Bank of Israel is scheduled to announce July rates on June 23.

Reuter added that demand for unlinked bonds was also up because inflation in the coming months is expected to be low. "There is a sharp drop in inflation expectations, which are now under nine percent," Reuter said.
But expectations of falling yields due to a tighter supply of bonds also affected trading on Sunday.
"There are far more bond redemptions than issues," said a trader. "This phenomenon is affecting both CPI-linked bonds and unlinked bonds."
Three months of budget surpluses and increased privatisation revenues have enabled the government to raise less debt, traders said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
